review.mathematics: Example 17: A is the union of the two horizontal closed edges in I times I. A continuous f:A to R squared has a continuous extension F across the normal square. Thus any two paths in R squared are freely homotopic; no endpoint-fixing condition is stated.

Top/bottom paths are sampled as native curves; the two connecting sides and interior deformation form a continuous illustrative extension.

limits: The book supplies generic curves without analytic formulas. The cubic path samplers and continuous t(1-t) interior deformation are Style realizations, not formulas attributed to the source.
Caller samplers can represent other continuous paths; finite sampled contours are schematic, and filling arbitrary folded map images is not claimed.
There are no imposed equal endpoints or fixed-endpoint homotopy claims.

review.adaptation: Vector lettering and consistent pale orange neighborhood fills
limits: The default Substance supplies one explicit finite partition; the ellipsis hides actual intermediate indices and does not assert a finite representation of the entire directed family.
Clean vector type and strokes replace scanned lettering; the source-defined partition order is not silently reversed.

review.mathematics: For distinct unseparable x,y in a non-T2 space, the directed product of their neighborhood systems indexes a selector choosing s(U,V) in every U∩V; its net converges to both x and y. The drawn value is one witness distinct from this all-neighborhood hypothesis.

The all-neighborhood selection property is declared as a mathematical hypothesis, not inferred from the one depicted value.

review.mathematics: Proposition 5, Lindelof implies separable in a metric space. Its argument starts on supplied printed 148 and continues on supplied printed 149: take a maximal subset E with D(a,b)>=p for distinct a,b, let V be the complement of the union of Cl N(a,p/4), and cover X by V and all N(a,p/2). Each center forces its own covering half-ball to remain, so Lindelof makes E countable.
review.visual: The original three-by-three array of hatched closed quarter-ball representations with nine black center marks. Original V, Cl N(a,p/4) and central a labels. No additional outer half-ball outlines are introduced.
review.adaptation: Consistent pale orange hatching and vector labels
limits: The displayed grid is a finite schematic prefix of generic E and does not assert that E is finite or a lattice.
The scan does not use one numerical metric scale for both center spacing and p/4 disk radii. Pixel positions stay in Style and do not become mathematical distances.
The circles illustrate closures of generic metric neighborhoods; they do not assert that closures equal closed metric balls in every metric space.

Assuming interior proposed supremum u belongs to T, add a cover element U_i prime containing u. Openness then extends finite cover reach beyond u, contradicting the upper-bound hypothesis. The definition and Case 1 begin on supplied printed 152.

review.mathematics: Proposition 11 and its supplied proof opening state that a compact subset A of a T2 space is closed. The outside x must have a neighborhood avoiding A. The printed continuation page 157 is missing. The visible graphic names paired V_y and U_y neighborhoods, their cover union V and the intersection U.
review.visual: Two source panels retained within one framed native SVG: overlapping neighborhoods around hatched compact A, and a separate common neighborhood around the marked outside x. Original A, V, V_y1, V_yn, y1, yn, U, U_y1, U_yn and x labels and their white knockouts. The two named cover neighborhoods use crossing hatching. Four nested native clip masks produce a true common hatch intersection of the depicted outside neighborhood contours.

limits: Smooth contours approximate the scanned irregular boundaries. Hatch density is lighter, with the consistent subdued orange fill.

The finite family and n labels are schematic: six chosen witnesses illustrate the compact subcover, and the right panel shows representative neighborhood contours rather than asserting the count of distinct sets from line loops.

figures.description: A compact cylinder I×C with boundary circles {0}×C and {1}×C, a side fiber I×{x}, and marked endpoint coordinates.

panels.description: The compact cylinder obtained as the product of a circle and [0,1].

review.mathematics: The graphic uses the factor order I×C, matching its boundary-fiber labels; the preceding prose also names the homeomorphic product C×I. The top and bottom fibers are {1}×C and {0}×C, and the marked side fiber is I×{x}. Both factor topologies and the product topology are declared compact; fibers are compact subsets of the product. The representative x is checked against the circle equation; native render tests verify its projected point lies exactly on the upper ellipse.
review.visual: One cylinder panel, full solid top and bottom ellipses, upright side edges and all five source labels are preserved. The two upper marked points, right endpoint numerals and left interval-fiber label follow the source composition. Only the lateral surface receives restrained orange shading; the endpoint openings stay white. The source intentionally exposes the full lower ellipse. The view preserves this wireframe occlusion convention, rather than hiding its far arc.
review.adaptation: Consistent restrained orange shading and vector lettering.
limits: The scanned contours are slightly irregular; the native ellipses are exact.

figures.description: A compact torus C×C with the fibers C×{x} and {x}×C, dashed transverse circle, narrow meridian and their shared marked point x.

panels.description: Compactness of the product of two circles, represented by a torus.

review.mathematics: The compact product C×C contains {x}×C and C×{x}. Their shared point is the ordered pair (x,x), distinct from the factor point x; all three memberships are explicit.
review.visual: Source outer ring, central opening, dashed transverse ellipse, narrow front meridian with a dashed back half, both fiber labels and shared point retained. Analytic outer torus silhouette closes sampled contour gaps.
review.adaptation: Consistent restrained orange surface shading and vector lettering.
limits: The source uses schematic projected fiber glyphs: an ellipse and a widened meridian. Their marked intersection is preserved without claiming an exact analytical latitude of the embedded torus.
The product point is labeled x as in the figure, while its ordered-pair meaning is explicit in the Substance.
The native 1536-patch surface uses restrained diffuse shading; scanned outlines are regularized.

figures.description: The compact cube I³ has its first-coordinate-zero and third-coordinate-one faces hatched, with a left-pointing bent leader and closed endpoints 0 and 1.

panels.description: The compact product [0,1]^3 is represented as a cube.

review.mathematics: The cube is the iterated product (I×I)×I; its topology is the iterated product of compact interval topologies. The marked left face fixes the first coordinate to zero: {0}×I×I. The marked top face fixes the third coordinate to one: I×I×{1}. Both faces are asserted compact subsets of the cube, and the lower/upper endpoint singletons preserve the closed interval boundaries.
review.visual: One cube panel with all twelve solid wireframe edges and its original oblique projection is preserved. The left face has dense vertical hatching; the top has diagonal hatching and the source’s additional vertical crosshatching near its back vertex. The bent leader points left into the first-coordinate-zero face, matching the source arrow direction. Both face labels have white knockouts; the 0 and 1 numerals remain at the front left vertical edge. Pale orange fill is confined to the two marked faces.
review.adaptation: Consistent restrained orange shading and vector lettering.
limits: The source uses slightly nonparallel scanned edges; the view uses an affine oblique projection.
Annotation dragging changes layout while the compact product and boundary-face geometry stay fixed.
